Hi Kimberly,

We're preparing for an upcoming third-party audit and need to understand Redwood's capabilities for audit/access log preservation and bulk export. A few specific questions below — if you can loop in the compliance/engineering folks that would be great.

1) Retention windows: what are the default retention windows for access/audit logs on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Can you provide options (90d, 1y, multi-year)?

2) Export scope & format: can we get a full raw export (request metadata, actor, resource, response codes, IPs, timestamps, request/response headers) in a machine-readable format? What formats do you support (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet)?

3) Export window limits: for a hosted account that currently has 90-day retention, is it possible to request a bulk export covering the last 365 days (for audit purposes) or are we limited to the configured retention snapshot?

4) Residency: if we require all exported artefacts to remain in EU-only storage, can you deliver exports from an EU-only endpoint and guarantee no US transit? Also how does region selection work for Dedicated/Private?

5) Deletion / DSAR coordination: after export, we will likely request deletion of certain logs under our retention policy. Do you provide a deletion manifest and a signed attestation (time-stamped) proving deletion?

6) Delivery mechanism, security, and SLA: what are the delivery methods (SFTP, presigned S3 + SSE-KMS, secure Drive), do you support customer-managed KMS keys, and what's the usual SLA for bulk export delivery? Is expedited processing available?

If easier I can share a short export spec — attaching our preferred fields.

Thanks,

Diane — thanks, answered inline below. Attaching a small sample export + a short spec for fields we typically provide (audit_export_spec.xlsx, sample-ndjson.gz).

1) Retention windows
- Hosted (default): 90 days. Customers on Hosted can request retention extensions up to 365 days via an add-on (subject to capacity & compliance review).
- Dedicated: retention is configurable; typical options we support out-of-the-box are 90d, 365d, and 730d. We can provision longer windows with a backup/archival plan.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): fully customer-configurable; retention depends on customer-managed storage sizing.

2) Export scope & format
- We can produce full raw audit exports containing: timestamp, actor id/email, request id, route, request metadata (method, path, headers), response status, response metadata, client IP, region, and associated tokens/keys (token ids only — not raw secrets).
- Formats supported: NDJSON (preferred for raw events), gzipped NDJSON (.ndjson.gz), CSV for flattened metadata extracts, and Parquet on request for analytics pipelines.
- We also include an export manifest (SHA256 checksums, export start/end times, record counts).

3) Export window limits
- Exports are bounded by the retention window configured for the environment. For a Hosted tenant with a 90-day retention, we cannot export beyond the retained window unless you previously requested and we archived longer-term snapshots.
- If you need 365 days and you are currently on 90d Hosted, options:
  a) If the historical data still exists in our backup (rare for Hosted), we can surface a one-time archive export (requires justification + extended SLA; best-effort).
  b) Upgrade to a retention add-on for future coverage and request gated historical restoration (subject to backup availability).
- For Dedicated/Private where retention was set to 365d, exports can cover that configured period or longer if archival snapshots were kept.

4) Residency
- Export generation happens in the region where the logs are resident. For EU-residency customers we produce the export entirely within EU infrastructure and deliver to EU-only endpoints (EU SFTP, EU S3 bucket). We maintain no US transit for the export files when EU-only is requested.
- For Dedicated the customer controls region selection; Private follows your on-prem/VPC constraints.

5) Deletion / DSAR coordination
- After an export we can execute deletion requests per your retention policy. We produce a deletion manifest and a signed attestation (time-stamped, signed by our Compliance team) listing deleted object identifiers and the deletion timestamp. For Hosted accounts, permanent deletions follow our deletion pipeline; for Dedicated/Private we can coordinate a joint-run deletion and provide logs of the deletion job.

6) Delivery mechanism, security, and SLA
- Delivery methods: SFTP (enterprise endpoint), presigned S3 URL with SSE-KMS (SSE-KMS with customer-managed keys supported), or enterprise secure Drive (encrypted).
- Customer-managed KMS keys: supported for S3 exports and for encrypting export-at-rest for Dedicated/private. For Hosted presigned URLs we can accept uploads to a customer-controlled bucket with SSE-KMS.
- SLA: standard bulk export ETA is 72 hours from the time the export job is approved. Expedited processing (24–48 hours) can be requested under our enterprise SLA (subject to capacity and additional fee).
- Checksums & verification: every export includes SHA256 checksums and an export manifest; we can provide GPG-signed manifests on request.

Operational notes / next steps
- To proceed please share: account id, date range, export format preference (ndjson.gz recommended), residency constraint (EU-only), and delivery method + KMS details if applicable.
- Attached: audit_export_spec.xlsx (fields mapping) and sample-ndjson.gz (small sample of format).

Regards,
